# Toronto Apartment Move-Out Checklist for 2026-08-31

A practical move-out plan for a 2-year tenancy in Toronto, focused on leaving the unit inspection-ready and reducing deposit disputes. I’m assuming the “security deposit” is being treated as a refundable deposit by the landlord; in Ontario, the common lawful deposit is usually the last month’s rent deposit, not a damage deposit.

## Move-Out Plan and Inspection Prep

| Timing | Task | What to do | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6-8 weeks before | Review lease and condition | Re-read move-in condition notes, pet clauses, key return rules, and any cleaning obligations | You know what the landlord can reasonably expect |
| 4-6 weeks before | Give written notice if required | Confirm the end date and submit notice in writing if your tenancy type requires it | No confusion about vacancy date |
| 2-3 weeks before | Start deep cleaning | Clean room by room; patch small nail holes only if allowed | Less last-minute work |
| 1 week before | Document the unit | Take timestamped photos and video of every room, appliances, fixtures, and any existing wear | Evidence for deposit discussions |
| 1-2 days before | Final sweep | Remove all belongings, clean floors, empty fridge, test lights, and confirm keys/fobs | Ready for handover |
| Handover day | Walk-through and return items | Meet landlord/agent if possible, return all keys, fobs, remotes, parking passes, and get written confirmation | Clear end-of-tenancy record |

## Room-by-Room Cleaning Checklist

### Entryway, Hallways, and Closets
- Vacuum and mop floors, including edges and corners
- Wipe baseboards, light switches, door handles, and closet shelves
- Remove scuffs from walls where possible with a gentle cleaner
- Check closets for forgotten items, dust, and hangers
- Clean inside of front door and any mirrored surfaces

### Living Room
- Dust ceiling corners, vents, blinds, shelves, and trim
- Clean windows, sills, tracks, and any balcony door glass
- Vacuum upholstery if included, and remove pet hair from fabric surfaces
- Spot-clean walls carefully; do not repaint unless approved
- Check under and behind furniture for debris, coins, and trash

### Kitchen
- Clean inside, outside, and top of fridge; defrost if needed and allowed
- Wipe oven, stovetop, range hood, backsplash, and drip trays
- Clean microwave, dishwasher exterior, sink, faucet, and cabinet fronts
- Empty and sanitize cupboards, drawers, and pantry shelves
- Remove grease from walls, switches, and handles
- Take out all food, trash, and recyclables
- Clean under appliances if accessible and safe

### Bathroom
- Scrub toilet, seat, tank exterior, sink, tub, shower walls, and grout
- Remove soap scum, mildew, and hard-water marks
- Clean mirror, vanity, faucet, and cabinet interiors
- Wipe vents, baseboards, and towel bars
- Check and clear drains of hair and residue
- Replace empty toilet paper holders or broken small accessories if they were part of the unit

### Bedrooms
- Vacuum or mop floors and clean corners
- Dust blinds, windowsills, closet rods, shelves, and light fixtures
- Remove nail hooks, if permitted, and patch tiny holes neatly
- Clean inside drawers and under bed areas
- Wipe marks from doors and around handles

### Laundry Area, Storage, Balcony, and Utility Spaces
- Clean washer/dryer lint traps, surfaces, and detergent residue
- Wipe shelves, utility closet floors, and visible pipes
- Sweep balcony, remove planters, dirt, and debris
- Check for water stains, leaks, or damage and photograph them
- Remove all personal items from storage lockers and parking areas

## Photo Documentation Steps

### Before You Start Cleaning
- Photograph every room from each corner
- Capture floors, walls, ceilings, windows, appliances, and fixtures
- Include close-ups of any pre-existing damage, stains, chips, or wear
- Save photos with date/time metadata turned on if possible

### After Cleaning
- Retake the same angles to show the finished condition
- Photograph inside appliances, cupboards, closets, drains, and under sinks
- Take clear images of returned keys, fobs, remotes, parking passes, and mail keys
- Record a short walk-through video if you want extra proof of condition

### At Handover
- Ask for a signed receipt or email confirming key return and vacancy date
- Photograph the final empty unit if the landlord allows a quick last look
- Keep copies of messages, cleaning receipts, and any repair invoices

## Notice and Handover Timeline for a 2026-08-31 Lease End

### 8 Weeks Out: Early Prep
- Confirm the exact lease end date and notice rules
- Review what items must be returned with the unit
- Start gathering cleaning supplies, patch materials, and photo storage

### 4-6 Weeks Out: Formal Notice and Scheduling
- Send notice in writing if required under your tenancy arrangement
- Ask for a move-out inspection appointment near the end date
- Arrange elevator booking, moving truck, and disposal if needed

### 2 Weeks Out: Declutter and Deep Clean
- Donate, sell, or discard unneeded items
- Begin kitchen and bathroom deep cleaning
- Repair minor issues you are responsible for, if allowed

### Final 48 Hours
- Finish cleaning all rooms
- Remove all trash and food
- Defrost fridge if needed and permitted
- Confirm utility shutoff timing and mail forwarding

### Move-Out Day: Handover
- Remove all belongings
- Return every key, fob, access card, garage opener, and parking pass
- Walk through the unit with the landlord or agent if possible
- Get written confirmation of handover and any agreed deductions

## Commonly Disputed Move-Out Items

- Unclean oven, fridge, or bathroom
- Nail holes, wall scuffs, chipped paint, or improper patching
- Missing keys, fobs, remotes, or parking passes
- Pet hair, odor, or carpet staining
- Burn marks, broken blinds, or damaged screens
- Trash left behind in closets, balcony, or storage areas
- Unreported water damage, clogged drains, or appliance issues
- Excessive wear beyond normal use, especially after a 2-year tenancy

## Toronto Deposit Protection Tips

- Keep the unit in the same general condition as move-in, allowing for normal wear and tear
- Do not assume the landlord can keep the full deposit without an itemized basis
- Save all written communication and photos in one folder
- If something is disputed, respond calmly and in writing with your evidence
- If the deposit is actually a last month’s rent deposit, it is generally applied to rent rather than treated as a damage deposit
